raw_response:
I have been farming this land for forty years, and chili is what I know best. My farm is only 2.6 mu, so I cannot afford to make mistakes — every plant matters. This spring I will rotary till the whole plot, because the soil here in Quzhou is heavy and chili roots need loose ground to grow deep. I will plant the improved yangjiaohong variety I bought from the seed shop, the same one I used last year. It costs a bit more, but the buyers at the market pay better for it, and my neighbors all say it is reliable. For fertilizer, I will spread about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting, and then topdress with urea when the flowers start to set. That is what I have always done, and it gives me a steady harvest. I have the well, so I will irrigate five times, especially when the fruits are setting in the hot months — the pump costs money, but without water the chili will drop its flowers. I also need to spray about fifteen times for insects and disease; the aphids and wilt come every year like clockwork, and if I am lazy for even one week, they will ruin the crop. If the weather is normal, I expect around 2500 kg per mu, just like last year.
